image.name: Portland Natural Gas Transmission System
aliases: Portland Natural Gas Transmission System, L.P.
image.description: Portland Natural Gas Transmission System is a standalone FERC-regulated natural-gas transmission business serving New England and Atlantic Canada. The approximately 295-mile system crosses New Hampshire, Maine and Massachusetts, connects with Canadian pipelines and has nearly 460,000 dekatherms per day of capacity. Its customers include utilities, energy marketers, industrial users and power generators. BlackRock- and Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners-managed funds announced the acquisition from TC Energy and Énergir on March 4, 2024 and closed it on August 15, 2024 for approximately US$1.14 billion including assumed notes. Regulatory evidence identifies BlackRock Global Infrastructure Fund IV and North Haven Infrastructure Partners III as equal 50% indirect owners through Beehive Loop AcquisitionCo LLC. The former owners' 61.7% and 38.3% direct interests ended at closing. PNGTS maintains a corporate office in Houston and an operating office in Lancaster, New Hampshire. No later company sale or signed pending exit was identified through August 23, 2026.

image.name: Revolution Wind & South Fork Wind
image.description: Revolution Wind & South Fork Wind is a paired manager-level record for two separate contracted U.S. offshore-wind project companies: Revolution Wind, LLC and South Fork Wind, LLC. South Fork is a 132 MW, 12-turbine project serving Long Island that entered commercial operation on March 14, 2024. Revolution is a 704 MW, 65-turbine project serving Rhode Island and Connecticut; it first delivered power on March 13, 2026 and was more than 95% complete in August 2026. GIP IV Whale/designated affiliates acquired Eversource's 50% interests in both projects on September 30, 2024, with Skyborn Renewables managing those interests. Ørsted retains the other 50% of each project, and Eversource is retained as the former 50% partner. BlackRock's acquisition of GIP closed after the project transaction and did not create a separate BlackRock ownership period. No later sale or signed pending exit was identified through August 23, 2026.

image.name: Rio Grande LNG
image.description: Rio Grande LNG is a large-scale LNG liquefaction and export terminal under construction at the Port of Brownsville, Texas. NextDecade operates the project, which is planned for approximately 30 million tonnes per annum across five trains and serves global long-term LNG offtakers. Phase 1 closed on July 12, 2023 with equity from Global Infrastructure Partners, GIC, Mubadala, TotalEnergies and NextDecade. The same investor group participated in later Train 4 and Train 5 transactions through separate project vehicles. XRG subsequently acquired partial GIP interests: 11.7% of Phase 1 and 7.6% across Trains 4 and 5. GIP remains an active investor after those partial sell-downs. BlackRock's October 2024 acquisition of GIP did not create a separate Rio Grande LNG ownership period. At June 2026, Trains 1 and 2 were 74.0% complete, Train 3 was 50.4%, Train 4 was 15.5% and Train 5 was 9.4%, with first Train 1 LNG expected in the first half of 2027. Train and holding entities are treated as project vehicles beneath the one terminal record. No signed pending company-level exit was identified through August 23, 2026.

image.name: Saavi Energía
image.description: Saavi Energía is a Mexico-based power-generation and gas-infrastructure platform serving wholesale, commercial and industrial electricity users and gas-services customers. The platform operates more than 3.7 GW across six combined-cycle plants, one solar plant, three gas-compression stations, three mobile turbines and a 40-mile pipeline. Actis formed Saavi from the InterGen México business in 2018 and sold 100% of the platform to Global Infrastructure Partners in August 2021 through GIP's emerging-markets infrastructure program. GIP remains the current legal owner. On April 27, 2026, GIP signed an agreement to combine Saavi with Grupo México power assets; if it closes, Grupo México would own 70% and GIP 30%. No legal closing was identified through August 23, 2026.

image.name: STRATOS
image.description: STRATOS is a direct-air-capture and geologic-sequestration infrastructure project in Ector County, Texas, owned through a joint venture between Occidental and a fund managed by legacy BlackRock Diversified Infrastructure. Occidental develops and operates the project through 1PointFive and consolidates the venture; BlackRock is the active noncontrolling infrastructure investor and committed $550 million at entry in November 2023. The facility is designed to capture up to 500,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide per year and use three permitted Class VI wells for permanent saline sequestration. Public sources do not disclose the owners' exact economic percentages, the BlackRock fund name, a separate STRATOS headquarters, or a legal commercial-operation date. No sale or signed ownership transfer was found through August 23, 2026.

image.name: The AES Corporation
image.subsector: Electric utilities and global power generation
image.description: The AES Corporation is a publicly traded, U.S.-headquartered power and utilities company with regulated utilities, conventional generation, renewable energy, battery storage and related infrastructure across the United States and international markets. Its customers include regulated residential, commercial and industrial utility users, corporate and technology buyers, utilities and wholesale-market counterparties. AES remained publicly owned as of August 23, 2026. A consortium jointly controlled by GIP-managed vehicles and EQT Infrastructure VI signed an agreement on March 1, 2026 to acquire 100% of AES through Horizon Parent, L.P.; CalPERS and QIA are also participants. Stockholders approved the merger and the HSR waiting period expired in June 2026, but other regulatory reviews remained open and no legal closing was found. GIP, EQT, CalPERS and QIA are therefore pending buyers, not current owners.

image.name: Coastal GasLink Pipeline
image.description: Coastal GasLink Pipeline Project is a 670-kilometre natural gas transmission project connecting northeastern British Columbia to LNG Canada’s export terminal in Kitimat. Its customers or end markets include LNG Canada and upstream natural gas production in the Montney region. The operating model is an asset-heavy transmission pipeline supported by long-term transportation arrangements rather than merchant commodity exposure. Operations are concentrated in British Columbia along the Dawson Creek-to-Kitimat corridor. Public materials indicate route length of 670 kilometres and design capacity of approximately 2.1 Bcf/d. Current ownership includes TC Energy, which retained 35% when KKR and AIMCo acquired a combined 65% interest in 2019; AIMCo’s exact split has not been publicly disclosed.
